text: Godrick the Grafted is the most distant, weakest descendant of Godfrey's bloodline among the demigods, considered least powerful in terms of inherited divine power.
Godrick grafts the limbs of other creatures, people, and conquered warriors onto his own body to compensate for what he believes is his inadequate, weak inherited divine power.
Godrick claims to have trained under Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, though the game never confirms whether this claim is true.

Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, a human sorcerer and head of the Academy of Raya Lucaria, became connected to the demigod lineage by marrying Radagon after he defeated her sorcerers in battle and proposed peace through union; they had three children together: Radahn, Rykard, and Ranni.

Radagon eventually left Rennala and their children to return to his duty as Marika's other self (since Marika and Radagon are the same being), leaving Rennala in grief and effectively abandoned, though she does not consciously realize this.

Rennala is found in the ruined Grand Library, surrounded by loyal students, singing a lullaby while clutching an amber egg (containing a shard of the Elden Ring) given to her by Radagon as a parting gift, which she believes still contains him, refusing to accept his departure.
The students at the Academy of Raya Lucaria remain devoted to Rennala even in her grief-stricken, barely present state.

Before her madness, Rennala was a young astrologer who, after a chance encounter with the Full Moon, learned moon magic—a school focused on lunar energies amplifying glintstone power, studied through empirical investigation rather than Golden Order faith—and became head of the Academy of Raya Lucaria and one of the most celebrated and powerful sorcerers of her age, known as Queen of the Full Moon.
Sellen was expelled/exiled from the Academy of Raya Lucaria for conducting heretical, forbidden research into the primeval currents of sorcery predating the Academy's systematized magic.
Sellen's true identity and history with Raya Lucaria are revealed across her questline, showing she is connected to something older than the Academy itself.
Sorceress Sellen was one of the most promising sorcerers in the history of Raya Lucaria Academy and had a unique glintstone crown.
Master Lusat and Master Azur were other primeval sorcerers banished from the Academy, and both had their minds broken by glimpsing the primeval current.

According to Jerren, Sellen has killed many fellow sorcerers in her studies and was a longstanding enemy of the Carian family who had committed atrocities against fellow sorcerers; Jerren promised Ranni and Iji he would slay her.
Sellen was imprisoned in Witchbane Ruins by the Academy and the Carian Royal Family due to her forbidden pursuits.
The Tarnished can help Sellen transplant her primeval glintstone, essentially her soul, into another compatible body to free her.
Seluvis helped Sellen in some way when she was initially exiled from the academy, though Sellen does not seem fond of him.
Starscourge Radahn was regarded as the strongest demigod in raw combat capability.

Radahn learned an entire school of gravitational magic to hold the stars still and lock the constellations in place because his sister Ranni's fate was tied to the movement of a specific star, preventing an unwanted destiny.
Radahn held the stars still for centuries because he resented Ranni's choices and loved his mother Rennala.

Radahn, a massive lion-armored general, studied gravitational magic in Sellia, a town in Caelid known for sorcerers who studied stars and cosmic forces, partly so he could make himself lighter and still be carried by his small horse Leonard, whom he'd owned since childhood, rather than giving up riding him.
Radahn's soldiers have camped in Caelid since the Battle of Aeonia, refusing to leave or kill him out of love, waiting for a worthy opponent to end his suffering.

Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, son of Rennala and Radagon, deliberately fed himself to a god-devouring serpent and merged with it to become both human and serpent, presiding over Mt. Gelmir and turning Volcano Manor into a haven for rebels and assassins who reject the Greater Will's authority.

Rykard believed the Erdtree and Golden Order were a lie—that Marika ruled by force—and sought to resist and overthrow them by becoming immortal through consuming divine power rather than worshiping it.
Rykard was served by the Gelmir Knights, and the lava sorceries usable by the Tarnished were created by him, some derived from old Mt. Gelmir hexes.

Morgott and his twin Mohg were born Omens, bearing horns and talons considered abominations by the Golden Order, and were cast into the sewers beneath Leyndell as children, sons of Godfrey and Marika.

Morgott conceals his Omen nature and disguises himself as Margit to hunt those who threaten the Golden Order before they reach Leyndell, first confronting the Tarnished under this pseudonym at Stormveil Castle.

Despite being an Omen shunned and reviled by Leyndell his entire life and rejected by the Golden Order, Morgott eventually escaped his confinement in the sewers and dedicated himself to protecting the city and remains its most devoted champion, defending a throne he was never allowed to sit on.
Morgott's dialogue suggests he once attempted to claim the throne of Elden Lord himself but was warded off by the Erdtree.

Mohg is Morgott's twin brother; both were Omens cast into the sewers, but unlike Morgott, Mohg fully embraced his accursed Omen nature, choosing a different path and receiving the favor of the Formless Mother, the Outer God of Blood.

Mohg built the Mohgwyn Dynasty, a blood-soaked realm dedicated to the Formless Mother, and kidnapped Miquella, hoping to raise him to full godhood and become his consort to claim the title of monarch, since Mohg himself is not an Empyrean.
Malenia was cursed with scarlet rot from birth, marked by the God of Scarlet Rot, a corruption she had no choice in that eventually consumed her eye, arm, and leg.
Malenia, Miquella's sworn protector and champion, has never been defeated in any battle, including her closest encounter at the Battle of Aeonia against Radahn.
After the Battle of Aeonia, Malenia went to guard the Haligtree, her brother Miquella's abandoned sanctuary, in his absence, having given everything for his cause and still waiting for him to return.
Placidusax was the Elden Lord of a world that predated the current cosmological order established by the Greater Will.
Placidusax has two heads, one representing a dragon god who abandoned the world and never returned, for whom Placidusax has waited ever since.
Maliketh, the Black Blade, is Marika's Shadow, bestowed on her by the Greater Will as an Empyrean (similar to how Blaidd is Ranni's Shadow), described as her devoted shadow and puppy.
According to the Stone of Gurranq, Maliketh was a ferocious warrior whose name meant 'Death of the Demigods'.
Maliketh's Remembrance implies he was betrayed by Marika, though the details are unknown.
It is heavily implied that the Beast Clergyman found in Crumbling Farum Azula is Gurranq himself, and that Gurranq is Maliketh, the Black Blade.

Godfrey, originally a chieftain named Hoarah Loux from the Badlands and an extraordinarily powerful warrior consumed by a lust for battle, was the first human Marika chose as her consort because he was the best warrior in the world, needed to conquer resisting peoples; he became the first Elden Lord and led the wars that expanded the Erdtree's dominion across the Lands Between.

Godfrey served the Golden Order with absolute commitment and was exiled for having run out of wars to fight; afterward he reverted to being Hoarah Loux, wandering and fighting for the pure pleasure of combat while waiting for Marika's promise to be fulfilled.
Upon becoming consort, Godfrey took Beast Regent Serosh upon his back to quell his bloodlust and become more fit to be a Lord.

Godwyn the Golden, firstborn son of Godfrey and Marika, was regarded as the kindest and best of the demigods, noted for his nobility and warmth, and formed a genuine bond of friendship with the dragon Fortissax, before being killed in a way that destroyed his soul while his body persisted, becoming the Prince of Death.
Godwyn's incomplete death produced an entity called the Death Prince, combining Godwyn's lingering flesh presence with the rune of death.

Marika was originally a Newman (Numen), a rare people noted for unusual constitutions, chosen as an Empyrean candidate by the Two Fingers and brought from outside the Lands Between to become a god at the Gate of Divinity in Anor Ilim, serving the Greater Will as its vassal.
Radagon, characterized by flowing red hair which he reportedly hated the tint of, was Queen Marika's second chosen consort and a great warrior.
A statue in the Royal Capital reveals that Marika and Radagon are one and the same being.

Godfrey also fathered twin omen sons, Morgott and Mohg, who were hidden in the sewers beneath Leyndell because their crucible-like deformities were considered shameful; Mohg was told his crucible marks were shameful signs of corruption.

Ranni renounced her flesh and transferred her soul into a porcelain doll modeled after a mentor she loved, dying in the flesh on the Night of the Black Knives to preserve the freedom of her soul, allowing her consciousness to survive and continue scheming.
Ranni was an Empyrean, a candidate to become the next god of the Lands Between under the Greater Will; although not born a demigod, she became eligible due to Radagon's unity with Marika.
Ranni wanted to escape the fate chosen for her by the Two Fingers and refused to continue Marika's cycle of divine control.
Miquella envisioned a world without discrimination that would welcome those rejected by the Golden Order, including albinaurics, the misbegotten, and omens.
Miquella developed a theology of 'unalloyed gold,' a form of divine power independent of the Greater Will, and used it to grow the Haligtree as a sanctuary.
Miquella possesses a supernatural charm that compels affection from others, including demigods, which he has used deliberately to further his goals.

Miquella was cursed with eternal youth, forever trapped in a child's body, unable to grow into the mature form required for godhood; his goal, revealed in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, is to become a god of compassion and establish a new order free of the Greater Will by completing a ritual involving capturing Radahn's soul and placing it into Mohg's body.
Miquella's connection to St. Trina, revealed in the DLC, shows they are two manifestations of the same being, echoing the duality of Radagon and Marika.
Miquella's compassion was genuine, but his methods were controlling and manipulative in ways his good intentions do not fully excuse.
Mohg believed he was a devoted caretaker enabling Miquella's ascension and expected to be made his consort.

Nepheli Loux is the granddaughter of, and adoptive daughter to, Gideon Ofnir, the all-knowing leader of the Round Table Hold faction, who took her in when she became Tarnished after losing grace; she is also the adopted daughter of Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, who named her his heir even in exile.
Nepheli's questline involves confronting the horror of Stormveil's population being experimented on and turned into shambling creatures by Godrick.
Nepheli Loux loses faith in Sir Gideon Ofnir after learning he orchestrated the attack on the Village of the Albinaurics.
It is speculated that Nepheli Loux has ties to Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, based on sharing the surname Loux with Hoarah Loux and Kenneth Haight deeming her worthy to lead Limgrave.

Kenneth Haight is a member of Erdtree royalty and self-proclaimed rightful leader of Limgrave, owner of Fort Haight, who looks down on Godrick for his cowardly actions during the Shattering and for lacking proper lineage to rule.
After retaking Fort Haight, Kenneth Haight seeks an eligible candidate to rule Limgrave and eventually finds Nepheli Loux.

Fia, the Deathbed Companion, resides in the Round Table Hold, is empathetic toward Those Who Live in Death and considers herself their guardian, and offers an embrace that grants a buff and a debuff simultaneously.

Fia collects deathbeds, the moments of heroes' final rest, carrying them inside her body, hoping to eventually create the Prince of Death made possible by Godwyn's incomplete demise; she was driven from her home when awoken by the guidance of grace, and is devoted to the cause of those who live wrongfully in death, holding dying Tarnished in her arms out of compassion because she believed someone needed to.
A Deathbed Companion receives warmth and life from champions and then lies with the remains of an exalted noble to revive them, a practice revered in Fia's homeland.
Fia's champions include Rogier and Lionel the Lionhearted, a knight who claims to be her father.

By combining Ranni's half of the Cursemark of Death from the Divine Tower of Liurnia with Godwyn's half from D, Fia implies Godwyn could be reborn as the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince through her role as his Deathbed Companion.
The Tarnished is a being who once possessed the grace of the Erdtree, lost it, died, and endured a strange persistence that being Tarnished grants.

Melina walks beside the Tarnished as a guide, tending the Sites of Grace that serve as checkpoints across the world, offering fragments of information and a kindness that seems genuine despite being largely unexplained; she has no grace of her own and no permanent vessel, appearing only through temporary forms she chooses, as though existing at the margins of the world rather than at its center.

Melina's personal goal, only understood at the end of the story, is to sacrifice herself as kindling to burn open the Erdtree so the Tarnished can enter it; at the Forge of the Giants she does so, stating she does not know what she will become but does not regret the choice.

Melina describes herself as someone born at the foot of the Erdtree who was given a purpose by her mother, implied to be Marika; she can recall echoes of Queen Marika's past actions and words when spoken to at Sites of Grace.
Melina may be a child of Marika existing outside conventional demigod lineages, or a soul given form by the Erdtree, or a deliberate contingency created by Marika.

Melina holds contempt for the Frenzied Flame and believes its lord is no true Lord; if the Tarnished takes the Frenzied Flame before the event at the Forge of the Giants, she will leave and threaten to deliver Destined Death.
Goldmask's revelation, reached using the Mending Rune of Perfect Order, is that the flaws of the Golden Order come from the fact that gods are as flawed and fickle as the mortals they govern.

Goldmask sat in silence at the edge of a great ruin, working out the nature of the universe without writing anything down, believing the right person would understand without words; he is a famed scholar of Golden Order fundamentalism who does not speak, communicating instead through rhythmic hand and finger movements.
Goldmask once lamented that hunters of Those Who Live in Death had become fanatics who hunted merely to have an evil to fight.

The Dung Eater has committed atrocities against both the dead and the living, defiling his victims' corpses with Seedbed Curses to curse their souls from returning to the Erdtree, and wants to spread his personal curse to all beings and future generations in the Lands Between by gestating the Mending Rune of the Fell Curse, so everyone is equally defiled; he is a Tarnished who bears the heart of an Omen, as suggested by his armor.
entities: Mending Rune of the Fell Curse

text: General Radahn is described as 'the conqueror of the stars' and Malenia the Severed as 'the Blade of Miquella'.
Melina does not have a physical form and serves as the Tarnished's Finger Maiden in exchange for being taken to the Erdtree and later the Mountaintops of the Giants.

The White Masks at Mohgwyn Palace were abducted by Mohg, Lord of Blood, and turned into Bloody Fingers through a ritual involving his Omen blood; of the four White Masks encountered, only Varre was able to withstand and tame the accursed blood.

White Mask Varre remains loyal to the Mohgwyn Dynasty and tries to indoctrinate the Tarnished into it; at the end of his questline, forsaken by Mohg, he still calls out to him and blesses the Mohgwyn Dynasty as he dies.

Bloody Finger Hunter Yura is a samurai from the Land of Reeds who hunts down Bloody Fingers, some of whom have been swayed by Mohg, the Lord of Blood; his biggest target is Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger, a Tarnished he holds in high regard.
Yura warns that those who partake in Dragon Communion eventually lose their humanity.
Sorcerer Rogier was once a scholar seeking the truth behind the Night of the Black Knives; his pursuits led him under Stormveil Castle, where he disturbed a corpse and became afflicted with Death.

Unlike D, who sees Those Who Live in Death as a threat to the Golden Order, Rogier is empathetic toward them; finishing his quest reveals insights about the Night of the Black Knives before he succumbs to his affliction.

D, Hunter of the Dead is a devout follower of the Golden Order who hunts Those Who Live in Death, especially Tibia Mariners for their Deathroot, believing they violate the principles of the Golden Order and must be exterminated.

D has a twin brother, implied to be named Darian or Devin, with whom he shares the same soul and body; they have separate bodies and minds but cannot be conscious at the same time, and both found comfort in the Golden Order, the one order that did not consider them cursed.

D, Beholder of Death can be found slumbering in Siofra Aqueduct while D is alive, and grieving there if D is dead; he swears revenge on his brother's killer, whether it be Fia or the Tarnished, when given his brother's armor.
Gurranq, Beast Clergyman is a large beastman who hungers for Deathroot; D was previously in charge of hunting and providing Deathroot to Gurranq before the Tarnished took over.

Roderika is a Tarnished driven away from her home across the sea, and her cloak implies she was once royalty; she met White Mask Varre, who gave her the same advice he gives the Tarnished: to seek Godrick and his Great Rune at Stormveil Castle.
The men escorting Roderika at Stormhill were taken and sacrificed for grafting, leaving her guilt-ridden for being too afraid to join them.
Roderika moves to the Roundtable Hold and is trained by Smithing Master Hewg to become a skillful spirit tuner, staying behind with him even as the Roundtable Hold burns, to repay his kindness.

Smithing Master Hewg is a misbegotten chained and imprisoned at the Roundtable Hold, tasked by Queen Marika with forging a weapon strong enough to kill a god; he believes the Tarnished will become Elden Lord, stating so before losing his memory completely.

Gatekeeper Gostoc is the gatekeeper of Stormveil Castle who nonetheless informs the Tarnished of a safer side passage, while secretly following and stealing a portion of the Tarnished's Golden Runes each time they are defeated in the castle.
Gostoc holds contempt for Godrick, having been mistreated by him, and longs for freedom from his duties; when Nepheli Loux takes the throne, Gostoc is happy to return to his duties.
Boc the Seamster is a demi-human outcast who admires his late mother, a skilled seamstress; he was expelled from the Coastal Cave and had his possessions stolen by other demi-humans.

After the Tarnished helps Boc reclaim his Sewing Needle and Tailoring Tools, he offers to tailor their armor; the Tarnished can help him further by giving him a Larval Tear to change his appearance or by telling him he is beautiful, and he is grateful either way.

Brother Corhyn is a cleric of the Golden Order whose armor implies he once foretold an inauspicious prophecy; he leaves the Roundtable Hold in search of Goldmask, a scholar of Golden Order fundamentalism, acting as his scribe by translating his finger movements into written records.
Corhyn begins to question Goldmask's intentions after learning of his reservations toward the Golden Order.

Gowry is a Kindred of Rot disguised as an old sage and was Millicent's caretaker as a child; he found Millicent and presumably her sisters as babies in the swamp of Aeonia and raised them hoping they would become scarlet valkyries under Malenia, seeing the most potential in Millicent.
At the end of Millicent's quest, Gowry asks the Tarnished to help Millicent's sisters attack her, believing betrayal will trigger her to 'bloom'.

Millicent is a daughter of Malenia, sharing her mother's red hair, missing arm from scarlet rot, and swordsmanship style; due to scarlet rot, she does not remember her childhood with Gowry despite feeling familiarity at his shack.
After being cured with the Unalloyed Golden Needle, Millicent seeks out Malenia to help her resist the scarlet rot, but is ambushed by her sisters at Elphael before reaching her.
If defended by the Tarnished, Millicent reveals she knows what Gowry hoped she would become, then removes the golden needle and succumbs to scarlet rot to remain herself.
Irina is the blind daughter of Edgar, Commander of Castle Morne, who escaped the castle with her father's and attendants' help after the Misbegotten serving it rebelled.

Irina asks the Tarnished to deliver a letter persuading her father to leave the castle, but she is murdered before their reunion; the large sword found by her corpse implies an escaped Misbegotten from Castle Morne was her killer.

Edgar, Commander of Castle Morne, was ordained by Godrick and stays to protect the castle's Grafted Blade Greatsword even as attendants flee the Misbegotten rebellion; after finding Irina's body, he regrets failing to protect her and swears vengeance on her killers.
Edgar can later be found as an invader at Revengers Shack, and the Shabriri Grape he drops suggests he succumbed to madness from Irina's death.

Hyetta is a blind young woman who resembles Irina and can perceive light by consuming Shabriri Grapes; initially disgusted that they are human eyes, she accepts it as necessary to become a finger maiden, and mentions other beings with trembling hands and emaciated fingers have also given her the grapes.
Completing Hyetta's quest and helping her become a Finger Maiden reveals more information on the Three Fingers and the Frenzied Flame.

Shabriri is a mysterious figure calling himself chaos incarnate, inhabiting the body of Yura, who he claims willingly gave it up; when met at the Mountaintops of the Giants, he tries to persuade the Tarnished to become Lord of Frenzied Flame and shares information on the Frenzied Flame Proscription.
Ranni discovered her own full moon, Ranni's Dark Moon, and learned cold sorceries from the mysterious Snow Witch she encountered in the woods; she has held Blaidd and Iji dear since childhood.
Ranni defeated the Glintstone Dragon Adula, who then swore allegiance to her.

Ranni is introduced to the player in a tower in northern Liurnia, one of three towers belonging to her and her brothers, once her family's home before her father Radagon left to return to Marika; she appears as a young woman with pale blue skin and silver hair inhabiting a small doll body.
Ranni's retinue includes Blaidd, a half-man half-wolf sworn to serve her; Iji, an ancient blacksmith; and Sellen, a snow witch whose loyalty is complex.

Blaidd is the half-wolven Shadow of Ranni, granted to her by the Two Fingers when she became an Empyrean; his loyalty lies only with Ranni, whom he considers family, despite being an agent of the Two Fingers, and even in madness he continued to defy his fate and remain faithful to her.

War Counselor Iji is the only friendly Troll the Tarnished encounters, serving as the Carian royal family's blacksmith and as Ranni's war counselor, providing guidance on the lost city of Nokron; he has watched over Blaidd and Ranni since they were children.
Iji's Mirrorhelm implies he feared the consequences of his treachery against the Greater Will.

Preceptor Seluvis is a magic preceptor serving the Carian Royal family and currently aids Ranni in her search for the dark path, while secretly scheming to betray Ranni and add her, a demigod, to his puppet collection.
It is speculated that Seluvis and Pidia have a connection due to their shared affinity for puppets.

Merchant Kale is one of the nomadic merchants the Tarnished can buy from, acquainted with Blaidd who calls him a busybody; he describes the nomadic clan as spiteful, suggesting their summoning of the frenzied flame was an act of spite.

Witch-Hunter Jerren was originally a nomadic wanderer who became a guest of the Carian royal family, befriending Ranni, Iji, and Radahn; he wields the Flamberge, a symbol of Redmane Castle, and heralds the beginning of the war festival when first met.

Thops is a glintstone sorcerer from Raya Lucaria Academy nicknamed 'Thops the Bluntstone' for lacking talent for powerful sorceries; if aided, he completes his lifelong project, creating Thops's Barrier, a defensive glintstone sorcery that deflects sorceries and incantations back at the caster.

Miriel, Pastor of Vows is a large turtle and steward of the Church of Vows who teaches Absolution though he does not require it himself; well-versed in the history of Rennala and Radagon's union, he teaches the Tarnished sorceries and incantations and, unlike Corhyn, is open-minded toward all sorcery and incantation scrolls given to him.

Albus is a first-generation Albinauric, created with defective legs that prevented walking, and when their legs fade, their life fades too; the Tarnished finds him disguised as a pot to escape Gideon's subordinates attacking the Village of the Albinaurics.

Latenna is a first-generation Albinauric and wolf-riding archer, one of many such archers, who was interrogated by an agent of Sir Gideon Ofnir (or possibly Gideon himself) about the second half of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, leading to the death of her wolf Lobo.

If approached with the right half of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, Latenna asks to be taken to Apostate Derelict in exchange for the location of the left half; there she transfers a birthing droplet to a large Albinauric named Phillia, related to creating life for the Albinaurics.

Ensha of the Royal Remains is Sir Gideon Ofnir's silent right-hand man; his armor set, the Royal Remains Set, and weapon, the Clinging Bone, suggest he is the reanimated remains of a king known as the Soulless King.
It is speculated from Gideon's dialogue that Ensha was tasked with finding both halves of the Haligtree Secret Medallion and attacks the Tarnished at Roundtable Hold to take whichever half they hold.
Tanith is consort to Lord Rykard and adoptive mother of Rya; she worked as a dancer in a foreign land until she caught Lord Rykard's eye and became his consort.

Tanith stayed by Rykard's side even after he swore himself to blasphemy and merged with the God-Devouring Serpent, even when his men turned against him and even when she was offered the Tonic of Forgetfulness as an escape.

Bernahl is an Ash of War teacher the Tarnished can first meet in Stormhill, said to be a Tarnished worthy of becoming Elden Lord, following his destined path without doubt, until his maiden threw herself into 'the fire'.
The Tarnished can later find Bernahl as a recusant at Volcano Manor; after Rykard is defeated, Bernahl denounces the Greater Will and vows to fell them on behalf of his brother.
Rya's real name is Zorayas, and she is a Man-Serpent disguised as a human working as the scout for Volcano Manor; only the Tarnished and her adoptive mother Tanith know of her true serpent form.
Tanith told Rya that she was born by the grace of a great king, but Rya later becomes suspicious of Volcano Manor's secrets and confronts Tanith.
A talisman left behind at the end of Rya's questline suggests her true mother was Daedicar, a woman said to have birthed multiple grotesque children through countless acts of adultery.

Patches the Untethered is a bandit who tricks unsuspecting people into death traps and entrapment schemes; if spared, he sells the Tarnished various goods presumably looted from the corpses of those he successfully tricked, and mentions his band of bandits is made up of foot soldiers and survivors of defeated armies left to fend for themselves.
Patches has taken a liking to Tanith and risks himself to obtain the Dancer's Castanets, hoping to restore her mind after Rykard's defeat.

Diallos is the youngest son of House Hoslow and lives in the shadow of his elder brother, Juno Hoslow; unlike Juno, a formidable fighter, Diallos is timid, which does not fit his family's bloodshed-focused motto.

Despite their differences, Diallos and Juno care deeply for each other, with Juno doting on Diallos and Diallos looking up to him; Diallos hopes to become a champion like his brother but grows disillusioned and seeks a different purpose.
Jar-Bairn is a young jar living in Jarburg, a secret village of peaceful Living Jars, and one of the few Living Jars capable of speaking to the Tarnished, a warrior jar like his uncle Alexander.
Jar-Bairn can be found talking in his sleep about reuniting with Alexander, poachers destroying the Living Pots at Jarburg, or Diallos taking care of him.

Iron Fist Alexander is an older Living Jar who left Jarburg to seek great battle and hone his skills; warrior jars like him are Living Jars filled with the remains of warriors, destined to leave home and journey alone to become great champions.

Alexander the Iron Fist is a giant jar, a living vessel called a 'jarhead' containing the remains of great warriors absorbed into it; found stuck in the ground up to his shoulders, calling cheerfully for help, he wants to grow stronger by absorbing the remains of great warriors.

Alexander travels toward the Radahn Festival out of genuine joy at the prospect of fighting alongside great warriors, and at the end of his questline requests to be defeated by the player so his absorbed essence can be carried forward.

Blackguard Big Boggart is a Tarnished and former criminal selling boiled prawns and crabs, first at the Boilprawn Shack and later outside the royal capital; he may have previously been convicted of thievery, having stolen Rya's necklace.
Boggart used to be cellmates with Dung Eater, witnessing him defile a friend's body with the Seedbed Curse, the most harrowing experience of Boggart's life.

Enia is a Finger Reader Crone the Tarnished encounters at the Roundtable Hold, interpreting the wisdom of the Greater Will through the Two Fingers; unlike other finger readers who become frantic after losing their Two Fingers, Enia remains calm.

Despite being an agent of the Greater Will, Enia supports the Tarnished burning down the Erdtree once her Two Fingers stop communicating with her, and claims that before the Tarnished, another person had gathered two Great Runes.
Vyke, a tarnished, was according to item descriptions closer to becoming Elden Lord than anyone before the player character.
Messmer the Impaler is Marika's son, born with an affinity for serpentine flame and cursed with the Abyssal Serpent inside him, who was erased from official history similarly to Godwyn's erasure.

Messmer remained loyal to Marika throughout his long war, never developing the perspective to question that loyalty; despite being abandoned by her, he continues his mission and becomes a dominant figure in the Realm of Shadow.
Royal Knight Loretta trained in a Carian royal combat school combining physical skill and magic, and devoted herself to serving Miquella's project.

Key NPCs met in the Realm of Shadow include Needle Knight Leda, a loyal follower of Miquella; Redmane Freyja, a former Radahn warrior; a Hornsent representative; and Sir Ansbach, a former servant of Mohg; early in the DLC it is revealed these characters were united under Miquella's charm, and when he breaks a rune arc to free them, the group becomes divided and uncertain, revealing his manipulative side.
St. Trina, an enigmatic figure barely mentioned in the base game, is explored further through interactions with her and her follower Thiollier, revealing her connection to Miquella.

Sir Ansbach is a former servant of Mohg, once part of the Pureblood Knights (though the crest on his armor has nearly faded over time), who now follows Miquella in the Realm of Shadow; despite knowing his loyalty to Mohg is neither logical nor just, he still holds onto his oath.

Redmane Freyja is a former loyalist of General Radahn, having fought alongside him in past battles, who has since become a devoted follower of Miquella after he healed a scarlet rot wound on her face, leaving a permanent scar she now views as her guiding compass and new purpose.

Freyja recalls fighting alongside Radahn and expresses readiness to fight again when first meeting the Tarnished, urging them to follow Miquella's footprints, the path she herself now walks, and feels a duty to understand and honor the vow Miquella made with Radahn.
Freyja reflects on the complexity of potentially fighting alongside or against former allies like Sir Ansbach.

Hornsent holds a deep grudge against the Erdtree, viewing it as an enemy of his people, and views Marika as a betrayer of his people; despite his hatred, he follows an oath to Miquella and offers assistance to the player, refusing alms or gifts out of pride but rewarding the player with maps marking crosses tied to his people's suffering.
After Messmer's death, Hornsent expresses satisfaction but states his thirst for vengeance extends to Marika and the entire Erdtree.

Igon is a broken drake warrior consumed by pain and a burning need for revenge against the dread dragon Bayle, having once sought honor through Dragon Communion; his soul clings to the mountain where his battle with Bayle took place, asking the player to climb the peak and continue his fight.

When the player defeats the Jagged Peak Drake, Igon reflects on the warrior he once was before asking the player to continue his fight against Bayle; after Bayle is defeated, Igon's spirit is freed and finally able to rest, his revenge realized.
The Dragon Communion Priestess compares Igon's ambition and hunger to Bayle's fiery spirit and relentless drive, and is herself a surviving Ancient Dragon and worshipper of Dragonlord Placidusax.

Moore is a gentle giant, a follower of Miquella, and a member of the Forager Brood, a group dedicated to finding crafting materials and recipes across the Land of Shadow; when the Great Rune breaks, he is visibly affected but continues clinging to his devotion to Miquella.
Moore provides Thiollier with Black Syrup after being asked to find it, and reacts with grief and anger if a member of the forager brood is killed or harmed, calling it an unforgivable tragedy.
After the final boss is defeated, Moore laments the loss of his brood and the absence of allies including Lady Leda, Father Dane, Sir Ansbach, Freyja, Thiollier, and the Hornsent.

Needle Knight Leda is the leader of Miquella's band of followers in the Realm of Shadow; she references Dane, a silent monk who has served Miquella longer than she has, describing him as reserved but a formidable warrior.

After the Great Rune breaks, Leda grows suspicious of her fellow followers and proposes eliminating the Hornsent, fearing his vengeance could threaten Miquella's cause, and identifies Sir Ansbach, a former commander of the Pureblood Knights, as a potential danger due to his past involvement with Miquella's blood blade.
After defeating Sir Ansbach, Leda reflects on the weight of her actions but accepts them as the price for ensuring Miquella's continued favor.

Thiollier is a non-combatant Tarnished character skilled in crafting poison rather than fighting, found at the Pillar Path Cross Site of Grace, who serves Miquella and mentions Lady Leda when first met, acknowledging shared devotion to the same deity.

After the Great Rune breaks, Thiollier becomes haunted by memories of St. Trina, the goddess of slumber, and longs for her poison to grant him eternal sleep, traveling south to find her resting place and becoming increasingly obsessive and erratic, eventually turning hostile if the player tries to speak for her.

Hornsent Grandam belongs to the ancient Hornsent race that once thrived in Belurat Tower Settlement and was connected to the Divine Beast Dancing Lion; he greets the Tarnished with suspicion, accusing them of complicity in Messmer's atrocities.
Dryleaf Dane is a master of unarmed martial combat, a devoted follower of Miquella, and a sworn ally of Leda.

Count Ymir is the High Priest of Manus Metyr Cathedral and a vendor for glintstone sorceries, sharing philosophical musings about the Greater Will, the Erdtree, and the world's flaws; his companion Jolán can be summoned during specific encounters once her questline advances.

Jolán is a loyal warrior serving Count Ymir, found standing on a pillar beside him in the Cathedral of Manus Metyr; she warns the player that crossing Ymir will bring regret, calls him a guiding star in the dark sky, and will fight to protect his will if he is betrayed or harmed.
Fire Knight Queelign is a knight loyal to Queen Marika, introduced in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, first encountered as an NPC invader in Belurat Tower Settlement and the Church of Crusade.
